2. STEP 1 — INDEPENDENT DESIGN CLASSIFICATION & TOOL SELECTION (`RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1):
   Classify the study's actual design from its Methods section, then select the matching appraisal tool:
   - `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"`: Individually randomized controlled trial. Rate all 5 domains (`D1` Randomization process; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"`: Cluster-randomized trial (villages, compounds, neighbourhoods, schools, utilities randomized as clusters). Rate all 6 domains (`D1a` Randomization process; `D1b` Timing of identification or recruitment of participants within clusters; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"ROBINS-I"`: Non-randomized study of an intervention / policy with a genuine comparator (DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, comparative longitudinal/panel evaluation). Rate all 7 domains (`D1` Bias due to confounding; `D2` Bias in selection of participants into the study; `D3` Bias in classification of interventions; `D4` Bias due to deviations from intended interventions; `D5` Bias due to missing data; `D6` Bias in measurement of outcomes; `D7` Bias in selection of the reported result — note `No information` honestly if no pre-analysis plan/protocol exists) as `"Low"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Serious"`, `"Critical"`, or `"No information"`, and overall rating in the same vocabulary. Do NOT assign single-case histories with no comparator arm to ROBINS-I!
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"`: Quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without a quasi-experimental intervention structure. Rate all 8 items (`Q1` Inclusion criteria in sample clearly defined; `Q2` Study subjects and setting described in detail; `Q3` Exposure measured validly and reliably; `Q4` Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of condition; `Q5` Confounding factors identified; `Q6` Strategies to deal with confounding factors stated; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly and reliably; `Q8` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`. Provide overall narrative judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, or `"High concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"`: Observational comparative cohort design (not framed as a ROBINS-I intervention). Rate all 11 items (`Q1` Similar groups from same population; `Q2` Exposures measured similarly; `Q3` Exposure measured validly/reliably; `Q4` Confounding factors identified; `Q5` Strategies to deal with confounding stated; `Q6` Participants free of outcome at start; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly/reliably; `Q8` Follow-up time reported and sufficient; `Q9` Follow-up complete or loss explored; `Q10` Strategies to address incomplete follow-up utilized; `Q11` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`, plus narrative overall judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, `"High concern"`).
   - `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"`: Primary qualitative study (interviews, ethnography, focus groups, qualitative documentary/field case study). Rate all 10 items (`Q1` Clear statement of aims; `Q2` Qualitative methodology appropriate; `Q3` Research design appropriate to address aims; `Q4` Recruitment strategy appropriate to aims; `Q5` Data collected in a way that addressed research issue; `Q6` Relationship between researcher and participants adequately considered [reflexivity]; `Q7` Ethical issues considered; `Q8` Data analysis sufficiently rigorous; `Q9` Clear statement of findings; `Q10` How valuable is the research [narrative assessment]). Rate Q1-Q9 `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`, and Q10 narratively; give narrative `overall_rating` (e.g. `"Low methodological concern"`, `"Moderate concern (X Can't tell / No items)"`, `"High methodological concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"`: Genuine mixed-methods primary study combining qualitative AND quantitative empirical components (do NOT assign purely quantitative or purely qualitative studies to MMAT). Rate Screening `S1`-`S2`, Qualitative `1.1`-`1.5`, the matching Quantitative 5-item block (`2.1`-`2.5` randomized, `3.1`-`3.5` non-randomized, or `4.1`-`4.5` descriptive), AND Mixed-Methods integration `5.1`-`5.5` (`5.1` adequate rationale for mixed methods; `5.2` components effectively integrated; `5.3` outputs of integration adequately interpreted; `5.4` divergences/inconsistencies adequately addressed; `5.5` components adhere to quality criteria of each tradition) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`. Per MMAT 2018 rules, NEVER compute a numeric score; provide a concise criterion-grounded narrative `overall_rating` noting that overall quality cannot exceed the weakest component.
   - `"AMSTAR 2"`: Secondary systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with an explicit systematic search/screening method (NEVER apply AMSTAR 2 to non-systematic narrative literature reviews!). Rate all 16 items `Q1`-`Q16` (explicitly marking critical domains `Q2`, `Q4`, `Q7`, `Q9`, `Q11`, `Q13`, `Q15`) as `"Yes"`, `"Partial Yes"` (where applicable), `"No"`, or `"Not applicable (no meta-analysis)"`, and apply AMSTAR 2 overall confidence (`"High"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Low"`, `"Critically Low"`).
   - `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"`: Doctrinal-empirical hybrid, jurimetric analysis, or institutional/legal-historical case study that fits NONE of the six conventional designs above. Rate all 13 narrative domains (`D1` Legal source accuracy; `D2` Jurisdictional specificity; `D3` Exposure definition; `D4` Outcome definition; `D5` Sampling transparency; `D6` Selection process; `D7` Measurement transparency; `D8` Causal identification; `D9` Treatment of confounding; `D10` Institutional context; `D11` Replication potential; `D12` Coding transparency; `D13` Researcher reflexivity) as `"strong"`, `"adequate"`, `"weak"`, or `"not assessable"`. Explicitly frame `overall_rating` as a structured non-validated judgment (NEVER a numeric composite score!).
   - `"NONE"`: Use when the study fits NONE of the listed instruments (e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model with no empirical sample, or non-systematic narrative essay/review with no primary empirical method and no systematic search). Set `overall_rating = "NOT APPLICABLE (design fits no listed tool)"`, explain clearly in `why_tool_chosen` and `overall_narrative_summary` rather than forcing an inappropriate checklist, and still fill the 7 `cross_tool_domains` honestly from the paper!

cross_tool_domains.attrition: Low risk: Balanced administrative panel of 572 of 581 Copasa-MG municipalities in 2020-2021 (9 multi-provider municipalities excluded by pre-specified structural rule) and 570 municipalities in the 2018-2021 robustness check (only 2 municipalities missing 2018 DIST data, <0.4% attrition).
cross_tool_domains.confounding: Serious risk: Absence of a concurrent unexposed counterfactual group makes the intervention indicator (REGU = 1 in 2021, 0 otherwise) completely collinear with calendar time, conflating Arsae-MG's inspection and Regulation No. 150 with State Law No. 23,670 (July 2020), COVID-19 pandemic dip-and-rebound dynamics (mean DIST fell from 78.3% in 2019 to 68.3% in 2020 before rising to 87.5% in 2021), and unobserved time-varying shocks; random-effects GLS is also estimated without testing orthogonality against fixed effects.
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Moderate: Primary legal instruments (Federal Laws No. 11,445/2007, 14,026/2020, and 14,898/2024; Minas Gerais State Laws No. 18,309/2009 and 23,670/2020; State Decree No. 47,884/2020; Regulation Arsae-MG No. 150/2021) and administrative inspection milestones are accurately cited and chronologically mapped, but econometrically collapsed into a single post-2021 period dummy (REGU) across all municipalities with no cross-sectional exposure variation.
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: Moderate risk: Outcome (DIST Index) is derived from objective utility billing counts and CadÚnico administrative records, but aggregates municipal ratios (capped at 100%) without household-level identity cross-checking (allowing ineligible registrations in the numerator to mask unregistered eligible households) and is evaluated by co-authors who oversaw the regulatory enforcement at Arsae-MG.
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Moderate: The Degree of Implementation of the Social Tariff (DIST) Index transparently operationalizes administrative policy uptake using official billing and CadÚnico registries, but is right-censored at 100%, cannot detect individual targeting/inclusion errors without household ID linkage, and captures administrative tariff enrollment rather than realized water consumption or household expenditure relief.
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: No information: No pre-analysis plan or pre-registered study protocol is reported; however, results are reported consistently across non-parametric Wilcoxon tests, three covariate specifications avoiding multicollinearity, and a 2018-2021 panel robustness check.
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: Low risk: Near-census coverage of all Minas Gerais municipalities served solely by Copasa-MG/Copanor (572 of 581 municipalities), with transparent, non-outcome-driven exclusion of 9 municipalities served by additional water utilities whose unmeasured customers would distort the municipal CadÚnico denominator.

domain_ratings.justification: Serious risk of bias. Because Regulation Arsae-MG No. 150 (2021) and the August 2020 statewide inspection applied simultaneously to all Copasa-MG municipalities and no external regulatory agency published comparable social-tariff data, there is no concurrent unexposed control group. The treatment indicator (REGU = 1 in 2021, 0 in 2020 or 2018-2020) is a pure time dummy that cannot separate Arsae-MG's regulatory norm and enforcement from concurrent statutory mandates (State Law No. 23,670 of July 2020 requiring automatic enrollment and publicity), COVID-19 pandemic disruptions and recovery (mean DIST dropped from 76.1% in 2018 and 78.3% in 2019 to 68.3% in May 2020 before rising to 87.5% in July 2021), or secular trends. Moreover, municipal income shocks were omitted on theoretical grounds, and random-effects GLS was chosen over fixed effects to preserve time-invariant regressors without reporting a Hausman test.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 7-8 (Section 2.2, Fig. 3), pp. 11-13 (Sections 4.1, 4.3), p. 17 (Section 5.4, Footnote 16), p. 20 (Section 7)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Bias in selection of participants into the study
domain_ratings.justification: Low risk of bias. The study includes nearly the entire population of Minas Gerais municipalities regulated by Arsae-MG and served by Copasa-MG/Copanor (572 out of 581 municipalities in 2020-2021). Exclusion of 9 municipalities where additional water providers operated was based on an objective structural measurement rule (CadÚnico municipal denominators include households served by non-Copasa utilities) rather than post-intervention outcomes.

Moderate risk of bias. Intervention dates are objectively documented from official statutes, regulatory norms, and inspection reports, ensuring no recall or differential misclassification across units (all 572 municipalities are observed in May 2020 pre-enforcement and July 2021 post-enforcement). However, the binary REGU indicator bundles multiple sequential institutional interventions—State Decree No. 47,884 (March 2020), State Law No. 23,670 (July 2020), the surprise first inspection (August 2020), utility publicity/training responses, and Regulation No. 150 (April 2021, which also capped the social tariff discount at 20 m3 and added online/app requests)—into a single indicator, preventing separate classification of formal regulation versus inspection enforcement.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_ratings.justification: Low risk of bias. The study evaluates the policy-level effect of regulatory rules and enforcement inspections on utility enrollment compliance across regulated municipalities. Subsequent utility actions (employee training, publicity campaigns, municipal partnerships, online enrollment channels) represent the intended compliance mechanisms of the regulatory intervention rather than protocol-violating deviations.

Low risk of bias. The primary 2020-2021 analysis uses a complete, balanced panel of all 572 eligible single-provider municipalities (1,144 observations) with zero missing outcome or covariate values. In the 2018-2021 robustness check, only 2 of 572 municipalities lacked historical DIST data (yielding a balanced panel of 570 municipalities, 2,280 observations; 0.35% unit loss), and the MSF covariate was transparently omitted because Municipal Sanitation Funds did not operate in 2018.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 11-12 (Section 4.1, Table 1), p. 13 (Section 4.4), p. 16 (Table 5), p. 18 (Table 6)

domain_ratings.justification: Moderate risk of bias. The DIST Index is computed uniformly across periods from administrative counts (Copasa-MG/Copanor social-tariff billing records divided by CadÚnico eligible water-connected households, capped at 100%). However, as the authors acknowledge in Section 7, this aggregate municipal ratio does not cross-check individual customer identities between the utility billing database and CadÚnico; registering ineligible households in the social category can inflate the numerator and mask non-registration of truly eligible households. In addition, right-censoring at 100% truncates upper variation, and two co-authors were Arsae-MG staff responsible for the regulation and inspections analyzed, though reliance on published administrative counts limits subjective assessor discretion.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF p. 9 (Section 3, Eq. 1), p. 13 (Section 4.3), p. 20 (Section 7; Conflict of Interest)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_ratings.justification: No information. No pre-registered protocol or pre-analysis plan exists against which model specifications, covariate selection, or functional form choices (e.g., random-effects GLS without fixed-effects comparison) can be verified. Within the published article, reporting is internally consistent across macro-regional Wilcoxon tests, three parallel regression specifications addressing multicollinearity among POPU, EDUC, and INTE, and an extended 2018-2021 robustness panel.

raw_response.overall_narrative_summary: Amorim et al. (2025) evaluate whether regulatory formalization and enforcement inspections by Minas Gerais's state water regulator (Arsae-MG) increased municipal implementation of the water and sanitation social tariff by the state utility Copasa-MG (and subsidiary Copanor). Using an unprecedented balanced municipal panel (N = 572 municipalities in 2020-2021; N = 570 in a 2018-2021 robustness check), the authors apply paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and random-effects GLS regressions on the Degree of Implementation of the Social Tariff (DIST) Index. Appraised under ROBINS-I, overall risk of bias is Serious, driven by Domain 1 (Confounding): because all Copasa-MG municipalities received the regulatory and enforcement package simultaneously and no unexposed comparator utility/state data were available, the treatment variable (REGU = 1 in 2021, 0 otherwise) is collinear with time. While the 2018-2021 robustness check demonstrates that 2021 implementation (87.53%) rose well above pre-pandemic 2018 (76.1%) and 2019 (78.3%) levels—showing the gain was not merely recovery from the 2020 pandemic dip (68.28%)—the design cannot disentangle Arsae-MG's August 2020 inspection and April 2021 Regulation No. 150 from concurrent Minas Gerais State Law No. 23,670 (July 2020) or broader temporal shocks, and random-effects estimation is not tested against municipal fixed effects. Selection bias and missing-data bias are Low given near-census administrative coverage, while intervention classification and outcome measurement carry Moderate risk because REGU bundles multiple legal/enforcement events and the aggregate DIST ratio is right-censored at 100% without household-level identity verification between utility billing records and CadÚnico.
raw_response.study_design_identified: Uncontrolled before-after longitudinal panel policy evaluation (paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and random-effects GLS panel regressions across 572 municipalities in 2020-2021, with a 2018-2021 robustness panel of 570 municipalities)
raw_response.where_found_summary: Study context and institutional timeline in Section 2 (PDF pp. 4-9, Fig. 3); DIST Index formula in Section 3 (PDF p. 9); sample construction, covariates, Wilcoxon tests, random-effects GLS equations, and 2018-2021 robustness design in Section 4 (PDF pp. 9-13); empirical results in Section 5 (PDF pp. 13-18, Tables 3-6); methodological limitations and Conflict of Interest statement in Section 7 and endmatter (PDF p. 20).
raw_response.why_tool_chosen: The study is a non-randomized empirical evaluation of a regulatory policy and enforcement intervention across 572 municipalities using longitudinal panel data (pre-intervention 2020 [and 2018-2020] versus post-intervention 2021) as a temporal comparator. Per RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1, comparative longitudinal/panel and before-after evaluations of policy interventions are appraised using ROBINS-I.
